Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api

Class Rule

java.lang.Object
io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule
public final class Rule extends Object
A rule: a condition that decides whether it fires, and an action that runs when it does, with a name, a priority and the language they're written in. A RulesEngine evaluates the condition during RulesEngine.run(FactStore), and fires the action when the condition is true and the engine's match policy selects the rule.

Fields:

  • ruleName: identifies the rule in error messages, exceptions and listener callbacks. Required, not blank, and unique within a rule list.
  • condition: an expression that must evaluate to a boolean. It can't assign or declare anything. Required.
  • action: an expression run when the rule fires. It changes the output object, which it sees as output. Required.
  • priority: higher values fire first. Equal priorities keep their list order, and a null priority sorts last.
  • description: free text for your own use. The engine ignores it, but listeners receive it.
  • language: the name of the expression language the condition and action are written in. null, the default, means the engine's default language.
  • enabled: whether runs use the rule. true by default.
  • validFrom and validTo: when runs use the rule, from validFrom (inclusive) until validTo (exclusive). null, the default, means no start or no end.
  • tags: names that group rules, such as a market or a product. A run given tags with RunOptions.withTags(java.util.Collection) uses only the rules that carry at least one of them. Empty by default.

A run skips a rule that is disabled, outside its validity window when the run starts, or without any of the run's tags: it doesn't evaluate the rule's condition or tell listeners about it, and its evaluation is SKIPPED. The engine still compiles every rule when it loads them, so a skipped rule's errors fail RulesEngine.load(java.util.List) too, and a rule that becomes valid later needs no reload. The time comes from the engine's clock.

A rule is immutable. Create one with builder(), whose build() rejects a rule without a name, a condition or an action. Copy a rule with a change with toBuilder(), for example rule.toBuilder().priority(5).build(). Because a rule can't change, the engine keeps the rules passed to RulesEngine.load(java.util.List), and listeners receive those same instances.

Reading rules from JSON: a binder builds rules through Rule.RuleBuilder, whose constructor is public for that. With Jackson, register one mix-in for Rule and one for its builder: 

@JsonDeserialize(builder = Rule.RuleBuilder.class)
abstract class RuleMixIn {
}

@JsonPOJOBuilder(withPrefix = "")
abstract class RuleBuilderMixIn {
}

ObjectMapper mapper = JsonMapper.builder()
        .addMixIn(Rule.class, RuleMixIn.class)
        .addMixIn(Rule.RuleBuilder.class, RuleBuilderMixIn.class)
        .build();
List<Rule> rules = mapper.readValue(json, new TypeReference<List<Rule>>() { });
The code is the same for Jackson 2 (com.fasterxml.jackson.databind) and Jackson 3 (tools.jackson.databind); only the imports differ, except that Jackson 2 reads validFrom and validTo, which are Instants, only with its java.time module: .addModule(new JavaTimeModule()) from jackson-datatype-jsr310. Jackson 3 reads them without one. A rule without a name, a condition or an action fails while it's read.

equals and hashCode compare every field, including description and language. A field added in a later release takes part too.

Security: conditions and actions are code, and what a rule can reach depends on its language: in MVEL, a rule has the same access to the JVM as Java code, including processes, files and reflection. The engine applies no sandbox. A timeout stops a run between rules and when an expression returns, but can't stop inside an expression that its language doesn't interrupt. Only use rules from trusted sources.

    • builder

      public static Rule.RuleBuilder builder()
      Returns a builder for a new rule. The rule is enabled, with no validity window and no tags, and every other field is null until it is set.
      Returns:
      A new builder
